places.name: Brăila
places.what: Born to Greek parents, Clearchos Xenakis and Photini Pavlou. The Friends of Xenakis add that the birth date is uncertain and may have been 1 May 1921.

places.name: Spetses
places.what: Attended the Greek–English school on the island of Spetses after his father took him from Romania to Greece; left for Athens at sixteen.

places.name: Athens
places.what: Studied harmony and counterpoint with Aristotle Koundourov, entered the Polytechnic in 1940, joined the Resistance in 1941 and was wounded in the fighting of 1 January 1945. He hid in Athens for two or three months in 1947 before leaving.

sources.title: Les Amis de Xenakis: Biography, 1938–47 entries
Varga, Conversations with Iannis Xenakis, 1996, pp. 13–19
Wikipedia coordinate record: Athens

places.name: Paris
places.what: Reached Paris in November 1947 on a false passport and lived there until his death, apart from periods of teaching and travel abroad.

sources.title: Varga, Conversations with Iannis Xenakis, 1996, p. 19
Les Amis de Xenakis: Biography, 1947 entry
Wikipedia coordinate record: Paris

places.name: Paris
places.what: Engineer and then architect in Le Corbusier’s atelier at 35 rue de Sèvres, until Le Corbusier dismissed him. Coordinates mark Paris, not the studio.

sources.title: Les Amis de Xenakis: Biography, 1947 and 1959 entries

Wikipedia coordinate record: Paris

places.name: Unité d’habitation, Marseille
places.what: At Le Corbusier’s request organised a spatialised concert on the roof terrace for the CIAM congress, with concrete music, Indian and Japanese music and jazz at three points. He had begun in Le Corbusier’s studio by computing concrete elements for the building.

sources.title: Les Amis de Xenakis: Biography, 1953 entry

places.name: West Berlin
places.what: Lived in West Berlin on a Ford Foundation grant from autumn 1963 to spring 1964. There he wrote Eonta and developed the distinction between outside-time and in-time structures and the theory of sieves.

places.what: Arrived to teach at Indiana University and founded a centre for mathematical and automated music; he resigned on 17 May 1972. He told Varga that he was at Bloomington twice a year, for three months each time.

places.what: Returned to Greece in November 1974, after the fall of the military regime and the passing of the law that annulled his sentences. His exile had lasted twenty-seven years.
